audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 matches a 48.41% lane Lucian owns outright until Ryze's first mana item, and the mirror left the difficulty fields alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Lucian, Lucian, Lucian, Lucian, Skill, Skill, Skill. The packet and the mirror both say Skill, Lucian, Lucian, Skill, Ryze, Ryze, Ryze — and whys[5] and whys[6] on this page already claim the lane tips to Ryze at first item and that he out-DPSes Lucian at two.
audit.why: Level 1 Lucian has one ability and no Lightslinger chain worth fearing; Rod of Ages and Seraph's are the real flips, which the captions already describe.
audit.corrected: Five matched pairs: rows 1 and 4-5 Lucian -> Skill, rows 6, First item and 2+ items Skill -> Ryze, with ratings 2/10 -> 5/10, 3/10 -> 5/10 and 6/10 -> 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six places say Relentless Pursuit 'dodges' or 'sidesteps' your W root (whys[1], whys[2], spikes[1], wants.foe[1], early, mid). Rune Prison is a targeted 615-range cast — a dash cannot dodge it. mid also states his E is 'roughly 14 seconds early on'; it is 16 at rank 1 and only reaches 14 at rank 5.
audit.why: Worse, the page misses the interaction that actually matters: Lightslinger grants Lucian bonus magic damage on his next two attacks whenever a nearby enemy champion is IMMOBILIZED — so your own root arms his burst. And every Lightslinger double-shot cuts Relentless Pursuit's cooldown, so counting the dash alone reads it wrong.
audit.corrected: Dodge claim removed everywhere; the real condition (an un-Fluxed cage only slows) stated instead; E written as 16s at rank 1 reduced by Lightslinger attacks; the immobilise-arms-Lightslinger interaction added to whys[1] and early.

edits.before: His Relentless Pursuit lets him sidestep your W root and punish the whiff — W is too valuable to throw at a mobile target with E ready.
edits.after: Rune Prison is targeted and lands regardless, but immobilising him arms Lightslinger's bonus damage — root only when you can finish the trade.

edits.before: Full E-Q-W loop is online, but Lucian's E still dodges raw W casts — open with Flux on a minion to mark him first, then root only when his E is down.
edits.after: Full E-Q-W loop is online, but an un-Fluxed cage only slows — mark him with Spell Flux first, then root while Relentless Pursuit, 16s at rank 1, is down.

edits.before: His Relentless Pursuit (E) lets him sidestep your W root and re-engage immediately after your empowered Q lands — trade only when E is visibly on cooldown.
edits.after: Relentless Pursuit is 16s at rank 1, but every Lightslinger double-shot cuts it — count his attacks, not just the dash, before you commit a full rotation.

edits.before: Use Relentless Pursuit to dodge your W root and reset into a second trade rotation immediately
edits.after: Trade Lightslinger double-shots to cut Relentless Pursuit's cooldown and reset into a second rotation

edits.before: Level 1 is pure damage control: Lucian's Q outranges every tool in your kit and his passive double-shot punishes any step toward the wave. Stand at Q range, last-hit, and let Manaflow Band stack on his poke rather than walking into his double-shot pattern. At level 2 you gain W, but do not spend it reactively — his Relentless Pursuit will dodge it and reset his double-shot, so you are down a root with nothing to show. Level 3 gives you the full E-Q-W loop, and the Flux bounce onto nearby minions is what makes this workable: E a minion between you and him so the mark clips his model, then W root when his E is visibly down and follow with two empowered Q casts. One full rotation on a rooted, Flux-marked Lucian hurts him badly — but if his E is up when you step in, abort, because he will dodge the root and walk back into auto range with Phase Rush nowhere near proc'd yet.
edits.after: Level 1 is damage control: Piercing Light reaches 500 and Lightslinger punishes any step toward the wave, so stand at Overload range, last-hit, and bank Manaflow on his poke. At level 2 you gain W, but do not spend it reactively — an un-Fluxed cage is only a slow, and immobilising him arms two bonus-damage Lightslinger shots aimed straight at you. Level 3 gives the full E-Q-W loop and the Flux bounce is what makes it workable: Spell Flux a minion between you so the mark clips his model, root while Relentless Pursuit is down, then chain two empowered Overloads. One rotation on a rooted, Flux-marked Lucian hurts badly — but if his E is up when you step in, abort, because he dashes back into attack range before Phase Rush is anywhere near proc'd. Bank the Manaflow stacks off his poke; they are what pays for level 3.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the grind: your mana costs are high pre-item and Lucian's sustained poke keeps you from walking up casually, so the lane becomes a CS contest. Track Relentless Pursuit's cooldown visually — his E is roughly 14 seconds early on, so count after every dash and use that window to step up for a Flux-W-Q rotation. Phase Rush on your combo gives you the speed to disengage after trading, which is the only reason this lane does not run you out of lane. At level 6 Realm Warp adds roam and flank threat but does not spike your 1v1 — do not all-in Lucian just because you hit 6. Instead, use the Warp threat to freeze Lucian in lane (he cannot leave if you can warp to fights) and farm toward Rod of Ages.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the grind: your mana costs are high pre-item and his sustained poke keeps you from walking up casually, so the lane becomes a CS contest. Track Relentless Pursuit — 16 seconds at rank 1, and every Lightslinger double-shot shaves it, so the window is shorter than the number suggests. Step up inside it for a Flux-W-Q rotation. Phase Rush on that combo is the only reason this lane does not run you out of it. At level 6 Realm Warp adds roam and flank threat but no 1v1 spike — do not all-in just because you hit 6. Use the Warp threat to pin him in lane, and farm toward Rod of Ages. Every recall should buy a Tear component before boots — the item curve is the whole win condition.

notes: The decisive correction: Rune Prison is a targeted cast and Relentless Pursuit cannot dodge it — the page said otherwise in six places. The real interaction, absent everywhere, is that Lightslinger grants Lucian bonus magic damage on his next two attacks when a nearby enemy champion is immobilized, so your own root feeds his burst; and his attacks reduce the dash cooldown, so his 16-second E is effectively shorter than counting alone suggests. Level chart brought onto the packet's and mirror's version in five matched pairs.
